audit.recode_to: quantity-sensitive, right-oriented trochaic (primary stress on head of rightmost foot: final syllable if heavy (CVC/CVV), otherwise penult; LL→ˈLL, LH→LˈH, HL→ˈHL, HH→HˈH, LLL→LˈLL), citing Joseph 2018 ch. 4 (pp. 289, 306, 310) and He 2025 — if the record is meant to describe Manchu as a spoken language (Sanjiazi/Ilan Boo, the only living variety under manc1252). If the record is deliberately about literary Written Manchu reading pronunciation, keep 'final' only as 'reported, disputed' with a caution citing Zakharov 1879's conflicting account and pending Gorelova 2002.
audit.reasoning: The classification 'fixed-dominant, final' rests on a single sentence in von Möllendorff's 1892 practical grammar of the written language; the quote is genuine (re-fetched sources and confirmed verbatim) but nothing was held and no page locator was recorded. Glottolog lists a 600-pp modern reference grammar (Gorelova 2002) that we have not read, and the 19th-c. sources themselves disagree (Zakharov 1879 vs Möllendorff 1892, per secondary summary). The two modern treatments of Manchu stress I opened — Joseph 2018 (Cornell diss., ch. 4, Čenggeltei's 1,500-item stress-marked Sanjiazi corpus) and He 2025 (OCP22, 2023 fieldwork with duration/pitch/intensity evidence) — both describe a weight-sensitive trochaic system with the rightmost foot carrying primary stress (initial stress in LL/LLL-type words, final stress only when the final syllable is heavy or under a sonority condition), and He explicitly

sources.citation: He, Songjun. 2025. A Metrical Phonology Analysis of Manchu Stress. Talk abstract, OCP22 (Amsterdam), University of Oxford. 3 pp.
sources.quote: 2023 fieldwork in Sanjiazi: Manchu is weight-sensitive (CVC heavy, weight-by-position for codas); moraic trochees parsed left-to-right with End Rule Right; /ˈsa.tə/, /ˈpi.tʰə.kʰə/ (initial stress in LL, LLL), /u.ˈlun/, /tʰu.lu.ˈkun/ (final heavy stressed), /ku.lu.ˈma.kə/; suffix /miə/ extrametrical; stress confirmed by syncope and by longer duration, higher pitch, greater intensity. Explicitly criticises Möllendorff 1892/Zakharov 1879/Gorelova 2002 for 'attributing stress to syllables in fixed positions'.
sources.note: Fresh 2023 fieldwork with acoustic correlates of stress in the last native-speaker community; moraic-trochee L-to-R + End Rule Right analysis; directly disputes fixed-position descriptions incl. Möllendorff 1892.

sources.citation: Joseph, Andrew Jonathan. 2018. The Historical Phonology of Manchu Dialects. PhD dissertation, Cornell University (367 pp). eCommons handle 1813/64967.
sources.quote: Ilan Boo (Sanjiazi) spoken Manchu, data of Čenggeltei 1998 (~1,500 items, stress-marked): closed and falling-diphthong syllables heavy; default primary stress: LL→ˈLL, LH→LˈH, HL→ˈHL, HH→HˈH; LLL→LˈLL, LLH→LLˈH, LHL→LˈHL, HHH→HHˈH; 'the head syllable of the rightmost foot bears primary stress' (p. 310); unstressed open syllables syncopate; regular final stress [..LˈL] when penult has a high vowel and final has /ɑ/ (bira → [bi.ˈrɑː]) (p. 312). Author notes (p. 61) the Manchu accentual system is the least well described part of the grammar.
sources.locator: Ch. 4 'Stress in Ilan Boo Manchu', pp. 279-330; default patterns (12) p. 289 and (25) p. 306; primary stress = head of rightmost foot p. 310; sonority-driven final stress pp. 312-313; p. 61-62 on the accentual system being under-described
sources.note: Only full-length modern analysis of Manchu word stress (Sanjiazi/Ilan Boo, ~1,500 stress-marked items from Čenggeltei 1998): quantity-sensitive trochees, rightmost foot primary — contradicts 'fixed final'.
